purpose: Try independently generated principal relations near the real norm roots, and distinguish ordinary integer relation dependencies from ideal two-torsion before claiming a strict Selmer class.
selection: On each frozen maximal-order binary cubic, all three ordered real roots alpha, denominators1..512, and m=floor(n*alpha)+shift with shifts -1,0,1. Keep primitive distinct(m,n) pairs in that order. Accept a value only if its remaining cofactor after stripping primes<=400000 has at most32 bits. Audit the first32 accepted values, plus the one previously certified box relation on the high fibre. No exceptional point or class input.
certificate: Exact root floors, norm/smoothness digest, full principal-ideal factorization including the fixed norm square factor, integer and mod-two valuation-matrix ranks, strict local kernel, and finite characters for any dependency products. A kernel is not a class-independence certificate; a strict class is not a rational-point certificate.
failure: Checkpoint both stages on both fields. Resource-limit failures stay UNKNOWN. No adaptive enlargement or parameter sweep.
